items.stem: Which of the following best describes "reflection"?
options: The transformation y = −f(x) (reflection in the x-axis) or y = f(−x) (reflection in the y-axis)
The squared graph: non-negative, touching the x-axis at the zeros of f
A transformation that moves every point of a graph by the same vector; y = f(x − h) + k translates y = f(x) by (h, k)ᵀ
A function with f(−x) = −f(x) for all x; its graph has rotational symmetry of order 2 about the origin
items.answer: The transformation y = −f(x) (reflection in the x-axis) or y = f(−x) (reflection in the y-axis)
items.markingKey: A. "reflection" is the transformation y = −f(x) (reflection in the x-axis) or y = f(−x) (reflection in the y-axis).

items.stem: Noah says that the graph of y = f(x + 6) is the graph of y = f(x) translated 6 units to the right. Explain the error.
items.answer: it is translated 6 units to the left
items.markingKey: f(x + 6) at x equals f at x + 6 (R1); features occur 6 units earlier in x (R1); translation by (−6, 0)ᵀ (A1).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why a horizontal stretch y = f(qx) has scale factor 1/q.
items.answer: A value f(a) now occurs where qx = a, i.e. at x = a/q, so all x-coordinates are multiplied by 1/q. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: A value f(a) now occurs where qx = a, i.e. at x = a/q, so all x-coordinates are multiplied by 1/q. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "y = f(3x) stretches the graph horizontally by scale factor 3." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: The scale factor is 1/3: the graph is compressed towards the y-axis.
items.markingKey: The scale factor is 1/3: the graph is compressed towards the y-axis. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Let f(x) = 3e^(−x²/4) + x/2. Use your GDC to find the coordinates of the local maximum of y = f(x), and hence write down the coordinates of the local maximum of y = 3f(x − 1) + 2.
items.markingKey: GDC maximum (A1 A1); x shifts by 1 (A1); y = 3 × 3.08 + 2 (A1).

items.stem:
The function g is defined by g(x) = −2 − 2/(x + 2), where g is a transformation of y = 1/x.
(a) Describe a sequence of two transformations that maps y = 1/x onto y = −2 − 2/(x + 2).
(b) The point (4, 1/4) lies on y = 1/x. Find its image on y = g(x).
(c) State the equations of any asymptotes of y = g(x).
(d) Find the y-intercept of y = g(x), if it exists.
items.answer: (a) vertical stretch scale factor 2 and reflection in the x-axis; translation (−2, −2)ᵀ (b) (2, −5/2) (c) x = −2, y = −2 (d) −3
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1 A1 (b) A1 A1 (c) A1 (d) A1 [Total 7 marks]

items.answer: Adding 4 outside f is a vertical translation 4 units up.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the order of transformations can matter.
items.answer: For example y = 2f(x) + 3 (stretch then translate) differs from y = 2(f(x) + 3) = 2f(x) + 6 (translate then stretch).

items.stem: Briefly explain why y = f(x − 2) is a translation 2 units to the right, not to the left.
items.answer: The new graph takes at x the value f had at x − 2, i.e. 2 units earlier, so every feature appears 2 units further right.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The new graph takes at x the value f had at x − 2, i.e. 2 units earlier, so every feature appears 2 units further right. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.answer: The inverse must map each output back to a single input; if two inputs share an output, the inverse would not be a function.

(c) Write down the equations of the vertical asymptotes of y = 1/f(x).
(d) Sketch y = [f(x)]² and state the number of local minima.
(e) Sketch y = f(|x|) and state the number of x-intercepts.
(f) Use your GDC to find the local maximum value of y = [f(x)]² between −3 and −1.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "reflection".
items.answer: The transformation y = −f(x) (reflection in the x-axis) or y = f(−x) (reflection in the y-axis)
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the transformation y = −f(x) (reflection in the x-axis) or y = f(−x) (reflection in the y-axis). Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The reciprocal graph: zeros of f become vertical asymptotes, and points with f = ±1 are invariant"?
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of graph of y = 1/f(x).

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A function with f(−x) = f(x) for all x; its graph is symmetric in the y-axis"?
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of even function.

items.stem: The point (−16, 2) lies on y = f(x). Explain why its image on y = f(4x) is (−4, 2) and not (−64, 2).
items.markingKey: f(4x) takes the value f(−16) when 4x = −16 (R1); i.e. at x = −4 (A1); horizontal stretch with scale factor 1/4 (R1).

items.stem: "y = |x − 3| has a vertical asymptote at x = 3." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It has a vertex (minimum) at (3, 0); there is no asymptote.
items.markingKey: It has a vertex (minimum) at (3, 0); there is no asymptote. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the graph of an odd function defined at 0 must pass through the origin.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: f(−0) = −f(0) gives f(0) = −f(0), so f(0) = 0. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Maya says that the graph of y = f(x + 5) is the graph of y = f(x) translated 5 units to the right. Explain the error.
items.answer: it is translated 5 units to the left
items.markingKey: f(x + 5) at x equals f at x + 5 (R1); features occur 5 units earlier in x (R1); translation by (−5, 0)ᵀ (A1).

items.stem: Explain why the graph of y = 1/(x² + 4) has no vertical asymptotes, and find its maximum value.
items.markingKey: x² + 4 ≥ 4 > 0, so the denominator is never zero (R1); 1/f is largest where f is smallest (R1); at x = 0, y = 1/4 (A1).

items.stem: Rafael says f(x) = 6 − 5x³ is odd because it contains x³. Explain whether this is correct.
items.markingKey: f(−x) = 5x³ + 6 (A1); −f(x) = 5x³ − 6 ≠ f(−x) because of the constant (R1); also f(−x) ≠ f(x), so neither (R1).

items.stem: The point A(−4, −2) lies on the graph of y = f(x). The graph is transformed by the following, in order: translation by (0, −1)ᵀ; then reflection in the y-axis. Find the image of A.
items.markingKey: apply each transformation to the coordinates in order (M1); (A1) (A1).

items.stem: Let f(x) = x² + x − 6. Sketch y = |f(x)| and state the coordinates of its local maximum and of the points where it meets the x-axis.
items.markingKey: reflect the part between −3 and 2 in the x-axis (M1); vertex (−1/2, −25/4) becomes a maximum (−1/2, 25/4) (A1); zeros unchanged (A1).

items.stem: The function f(x) = x² − 8x + 17 is defined for x ≤ c. Find the greatest value of c for which f has an inverse, and find f⁻¹(x) for that domain, stating its domain.
items.markingKey: vertex at x = 4 so c = 4 (A1); complete the square (M1); choose the negative root (R1); f⁻¹ and domain (A1 A1).

items.stem: Describe a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of y = ln x onto the graph of y = 2ln(x − 4) + 2.
items.answer: a vertical stretch with scale factor 2, then a translation by (4, 2)ᵀ
items.markingKey: a vertical stretch with scale factor 2 (A1 A1); translation (4, 2)ᵀ (A1 A1).

items.stem: Let f(x) = x² + 2x. For the graph of y = 1/f(x), state the equations of the asymptotes, the y-intercept and the coordinates of the local maximum.
items.markingKey: zeros of f give vertical asymptotes (A1 A1); f → ∞ gives y = 0 (A1); minimum (−1, −1) of f becomes maximum of 1/f (M1 A1).

items.stem: A student claims: "f(x) = x³ + 1 is odd because x³ is odd." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: f(−x) = −x³ + 1 ≠ −f(x) = −x³ − 1, so f is neither odd nor even.
items.markingKey: f(−x) = −x³ + 1 ≠ −f(x) = −x³ − 1, so f is neither odd nor even. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Describe a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of y = √x onto the graph of y = −√(x − 2) − 3.
items.answer: a reflection in the x-axis, then a translation by (2, −3)ᵀ
items.markingKey: a reflection in the x-axis (A1 A1); translation (2, −3)ᵀ (A1 A1).

items.stem: Explain why most functions are neither odd nor even.
items.answer: The conditions f(−x) = f(x) and f(−x) = −f(x) are special symmetries; e.g. x² + x has f(−x) = x² − x, which is neither f(x) nor −f(x).
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The conditions f(−x) = f(x) and f(−x) = −f(x) are special symmetries; e.g. x² + x has f(−x) = x² − x, which is neither f(x) nor −f(x). (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why points where f(x) = 1 or f(x) = −1 lie on both y = f(x) and y = 1/f(x).
